findings.description: Protocol title states "PHASE III CLINICAL TRIAL…" while body text describes a Phase Ib/IIa first-in-human safety study with exploratory efficacy. Phase III implies a large, confirmatory trial powered for definitive efficacy outcomes.
findings.recommendation: Correct title to "Phase Ib/IIa Clinical Trial" and ensure phase designation is consistent across title, synopsis, and regulatory sections. Align language with early-phase safety-focused design, not with Phase III confirmatory trials.
findings.actual_outcome: Would cause regulatory confusion; FDA/EMA reviewers could consider the study misclassified; funding agencies would question scientific rigor.

findings.description: Protocol states n=60 (15 per arm) is "not formally powered" for efficacy, yet also claims it will detect a clinically meaningful change in HbA1c without providing assumptions, variance, or effect size.
findings.recommendation: EITHER (1) Perform formal power calculation and specify assumptions, or (2) remove claims of detecting a "clinically meaningful" effect and explicitly state the trial is exploratory for efficacy signal and make safety the sole primary endpoint.
findings.actual_outcome: Reviewers would question study validity and interpretability; journal editors would reject for inadequate statistical rigor.

findings.description: No explicit exclusion for history of severe hypoglycaemia in the prior 12–24 months in a trial testing a glucose-lowering botanical in adults with Type 2 diabetes.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit exclusion for "severe hypoglycaemia within the last 24 months" (or 12 months if justified), consistent with hypoglycaemia risk stratification used in ACCORD.
findings.actual_outcome: If not corrected, increased risk of serious hypoglycaemic events in a small, first-in-human sample; ethics committees and DSMB would likely demand amendment.

findings.description: Protocol defines participants as "treatment-naive" but also allows prior metformin exposure up to 3 months with washout. This creates ambiguity in baseline treatment history.
findings.recommendation: Clarify whether truly treatment-naive patients are required or whether short prior metformin use is permitted. Align language in inclusion criteria, synopsis, and statistical analysis plan.
findings.actual_outcome: Heterogeneous baseline treatment exposure would complicate interpretation of safety and glycaemic effects.

findings.description: Multi-level dose escalation (500, 1000, 1500 mg BID) is specified without explicit stopping rules or clear criteria for halting escalation in case of toxicity.
findings.recommendation: Add a formal dose-escalation algorithm including cohort-wise review, predefined stopping boundaries, and DSMB oversight, similar to oncology Phase I designs.
findings.actual_outcome: Without clear rules, investigators could continue escalation despite emerging toxicity, increasing participant risk and regulatory concern.

findings.description: Hunteria extract standardisation is described only qualitatively (e.g. "standardised to active alkaloids") without specifying batch-to-batch assay limits or named reference compound.
findings.recommendation: Define quantitative standardisation parameters (e.g. % content of specific marker compound with acceptable range) and describe batch release testing.
findings.actual_outcome: Inconsistent product potency could reduce interpretability of both safety and exploratory efficacy findings.

findings.description: Primary safety and exploratory efficacy endpoints are assessed at 12 weeks, but HbA1c reflects ~3-month glycaemic history; early timepoints may not capture full effect.
findings.recommendation: Add a 24-week HbA1c assessment or justify 12-week primary timepoint with prior data on expected onset of effect.
findings.actual_outcome: Short follow-up could under-estimate effect size or mischaracterise trajectory of glycaemic response.

findings.description: Excludes participants with eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73m², which is stricter than many diabetes trials and may unnecessarily limit inclusion of stable CKD stage 3 participants.
findings.recommendation: Consider allowing eGFR down to 45 mL/min/1.73m² (with appropriate monitoring) to improve external validity while maintaining safety.
findings.actual_outcome: Primarily affects generalisability rather than internal validity; may slow recruitment if real-world population has higher CKD prevalence.
